lessons.title: Pre-Leased Property: Buying an Income Stream

children.text: A broker sends you a one-line pitch: "Pre-leased office, HITEC City, listed IT tenant, 7.6% yield, ₹3 crore." It sounds like the ideal commercial investment. No vacancy risk, no hunt for tenants, rent from the first month. But a pre-leased property is not really a building. It is a contract with a building attached. Its value depends on how much rent is left in that contract, how safe the tenant is, and what happens when the lease ends. This lesson shows you how to price one and how to check that the income is real.

body.text: When you buy a pre-leased property, you are buying the lease, not just the space. Price the rent you are guaranteed, the tenant who pays it, and the day the guarantee ends.

children.text: What Pre-Leased Property Is and Who Sells It

markDefs.definition: A commercial property sold with a tenant already in place under a signed lease, so the buyer receives rent from the date of purchase.
A transaction where a business sells a property it uses to an investor and simultaneously signs a lease to keep occupying it, turning owned real estate into cash.

children.text: A
pre-leased property

comes to market from three main sources. Developers lease units in a new building and then sell them to investors at a premium. Existing investors sell to free up capital or rebalance. And businesses sometimes sell premises they occupy and lease them straight back, known as a
sale and leaseback

body.text: In a sale and leaseback, always ask why the business is selling. A company raising cash to expand is a good tenant. A company raising cash because it is struggling may become your problem within a year. Read its financials before you read the brochure.

children.text: Pricing: Income Divided by Cap Rate
Pre-leased property is priced like a bond. Buyers look at the net operating income and apply the cap rate the market demands for that kind of tenant, lease and location.

body.latex: \text{Value} = \frac{\text{Net Operating Income}}{\text{Cap Rate}} \qquad \text{Cap Rate} = \frac{\text{Net Operating Income}}{\text{Price}}

children.text: Back to the HITEC City pitch. The 2,000 sq ft unit is leased at ₹100 per sq ft, so rent is ₹2 lakh a month or ₹24 lakh a year. The owner pays about ₹1.2 lakh a year in property tax and insurance, so net operating income is ₹22.8 lakh. At ₹3 crore, the cap rate is ₹22.8 lakh ÷ ₹3 crore = 7.6%. The listing's "7.6% yield" checks out, but only on net income, which is how you should always verify it.

stats.label: Annual rent
stats.context: ₹100 per sq ft on 2,000 sq ft

stats.label: Deposit held
stats.context: Six months' rent, transfers to buyer

children.text: Small changes in cap rate move the price a lot. The same ₹24 lakh of net income is worth very different amounts depending on how risky buyers think it is.

body.title: Value of ₹24 lakh net income at different cap rates (₹ crore)

children.text: Moving from a 7% to a 10% cap rate cuts value from about ₹3.43 crore to ₹2.4 crore, a 30% fall with no change in rent. What pushes cap rates up or down is mostly the quality of the lease: tenant strength, time left in the lock-in, and whether the rent is sustainable.
Under-Rented vs Over-Rented

markDefs.definition: The rent a tenant is actually paying today under the existing lease, as opposed to the market rent the space would fetch if leased afresh.

children.text: The most overlooked question is whether the current rent, called the
passing rent
, is above or below what the space would fetch on the open market today.

columns.label: Under-rented (passing below market)
points: Tenant has a good deal and is likely to stay
Rent can move up at renewal
Value tends to rise as leases reset

columns.label: Over-rented (passing above market)
points: Tenant is overpaying and may leave or renegotiate
Rent likely to fall at renewal
Value tends to fall as leases reset

children.text: Example: a 2,000 sq ft unit earning ₹150 per sq ft when similar space now leases at ₹120. Rent is ₹36 lakh a year, which at an 8% cap rate supports a value of ₹4.5 crore. If the lock-in ends next year and the tenant renegotiates to market, rent falls to ₹28.8 lakh and value to ₹3.6 crore. That ₹90 lakh drop is sitting inside the listing the day you buy it.

body.text: A headline yield well above the market is rarely a gift. The usual explanations are over-rented space, a weak tenant, a lock-in about to expire, or a building with problems. Find out which one it is before you celebrate.

children.text: Verifying the Income Is Real
Brokers and sellers present the best version of a lease. Your job is to confirm that the rent is actually being paid, on the terms stated, by the tenant named.

body.caption: Documents to verify before buying pre-leased property

cells: Registered lease deed
The legal terms of the tenancy
Rent, lock-in, escalation dates, exit and renewal rights, force majeure
Seller's bank statements
Rent is actually received
Regular credits matching the lease, no unexplained gaps
Seller's Form 26AS or AIS
The tenant is deducting and depositing TDS on rent
TDS entries from the tenant matching the rent amount
GST invoices and returns
Rent is billed and GST filed
Consistent monthly invoices to the named tenant
Tenant financials
The tenant can keep paying
Revenue trend, profits and debt; for listed tenants, check on Screener.in
CAM and property tax receipts
No hidden dues
Paid-up maintenance and tax, no disputes with the association
Title and approvals
The seller can sell a clean asset
Title chain, encumbrance certificate, occupancy certificate

body.label: Income Tax e-filing portal
body.description: Ask the seller to share their Annual Information Statement (AIS) or Form 26AS from this portal. TDS deducted by the tenant on rent appears there, making it one of the strongest proofs that the rent is genuine.

markDefs.definition: A letter in which the tenant formally acknowledges the new owner as its landlord and agrees to pay rent to the new owner under the existing lease.

children.text: After the sale, the tenant signs an
attornment letter
acknowledging you as the new landlord. Without it, rent can continue to go to the old owner, and disputes follow.
The Deposit and the Deal Math

body.title: How the tenant's deposit changes your cash outlay

children.text: The seller holds a ₹12 lakh security deposit that it must refund to the tenant when the lease ends. When you buy, that obligation moves to you. So the seller usually passes the deposit across, most often by reducing the amount you pay.

You pay ₹3 crore minus ₹12 lakh = ₹2.88 crore. On that cash, net income of ₹22.8 lakh is a 7.9% return. But the ₹12 lakh is not free money: you must refund it to the tenant at exit. Treat it as an interest-free loan from the tenant, not as a discount.
Also budget for stamp duty and registration on the purchase, and deduct 1% TDS from the payment to the seller, since the price exceeds ₹50 lakh.

body.label: TDS when you buy
body.context: When the price of immovable property is ₹50 lakh or more, the buyer must deduct 1% TDS from the payment to a resident seller and deposit it with the government.

body.title: Calculate: What Should You Pay?
body.prompt: A pre-leased office in Baner, Pune earns net operating income of ₹18 lakh a year. Given its tenant and lease, similar properties trade at an 8.5% cap rate. What is a fair value, in ₹ lakh? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Value = ₹18 lakh ÷ 0.085 = ₹211.8 lakh, or about ₹2.12 crore. If the seller asks ₹2.4 crore, the implied cap rate is only 7.5%, which would need a stronger tenant or a longer lock-in to justify.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Changing Landlords
body.textWithBlank: After buying a pre-leased property, the new owner should obtain an ___ letter in which the tenant acknowledges the new owner as landlord.
body.explanation: An attornment letter confirms that the tenant will now pay rent to the new owner under the existing lease terms.

body.title: Quick Check: Reading a Yield
body.question: Two pre-leased units in the same building offer the same rent. Unit X has a listed tenant with 5 years of lock-in left. Unit Y has a two-year-old startup tenant whose lock-in ends in 4 months. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Both should sell at the same price because rent is identical
Unit Y should sell at a higher price because its tenant may pay more later
Unit X should trade at a lower cap rate, and so a higher price, than Unit Y
Cap rates do not depend on tenant quality
body.explanation: Buyers accept a lower cap rate for safer income. A listed tenant locked in for 5 years is far safer than a young startup that can leave in 4 months, so Unit X deserves a lower cap rate and a higher price for the same rent.

body.title: Scenario: The 9% Yield in Salt Lake
body.scenario: Sanjay is offered a 3,000 sq ft pre-leased office in Salt Lake Sector V, Kolkata for ₹3.6 crore. The tenant is a co-working operator paying ₹90 per sq ft, or ₹2.7 lakh a month. The listing advertises a "9% yield". The lease is 6 years old, its lock-in ended two years ago, and the tenant can leave with 3 months' notice. Comparable space nearby now leases at about ₹70 per sq ft.
body.prompt: Is 9% a good deal? What is the property really worth?
body.modelAnswer: Rent of ₹32.4 lakh a year on ₹3.6 crore is indeed 9% gross, but the income is fragile. The space is over-rented: market rent is about ₹70 per sq ft, which is ₹2.1 lakh a month or ₹25.2 lakh a year. There is no lock-in, so the operator can renegotiate or leave with 3 months' notice, and a co-working operator's own income depends on its sub-tenants. Valuing the realistic market rent at the same 9% gives ₹25.2 lakh ÷ 0.09 = ₹2.8 crore, about ₹80 lakh below the asking price, and that is before allowing for months of vacancy and a rent-free period if the operator leaves. Sanjay should either negotiate the price down towards ₹2.8 crore or less, ask the tenant to commit to a fresh lock-in at a sustainable rent before closing, or walk away.

body.title: Pre-Leased Purchase Checklist
steps: Recalculate the yield on net operating income, not gross rent
Compare passing rent with current market rent for similar space
Note the remaining lock-in, next escalation date and tenant exit rights
Verify rent receipts through bank statements and the seller's AIS or Form 26AS
Confirm the deposit amount and how it will be transferred
Check title, occupancy certificate, CAM dues and property tax
Obtain an attornment letter from the tenant at closing
Deduct 1% TDS on the purchase price if it is ₹50 lakh or more

cards.definition: Commercial property sold with a tenant already paying rent under a signed lease.
A business sells a property it uses and leases it back from the buyer.
The rent currently being paid under the existing lease.
Passing rent above current market rent, so rent may fall at renewal.
Passing rent below current market rent, so rent may rise at renewal.
A tenant's written acknowledgement of the new owner as landlord.

points: A pre-leased property is valued mainly on its lease: net income divided by a cap rate that reflects tenant quality and lease security.
A few percentage points of cap rate change value dramatically; moving from 7% to 10% cuts value by about 30% for the same rent.
Always compare passing rent with market rent; over-rented space hides a fall in income and value at renewal.
Verify income through the lease deed, bank statements, the seller's AIS or Form 26AS, GST records and tenant financials.
The tenant's deposit transfers to you as a liability, reducing your cash outlay but not your obligations.
Headline yields well above market usually signal weaker tenants, short lock-ins or over-rented space.

body.text: Rents, cap rates and valuations in this lesson are illustrative. Tax rules, including TDS on property purchases, can change; verify current law with a qualified professional. This lesson is educational and is not a recommendation to buy any property.
